title: Keyboard and sound
objective: React to keys with keydown/keyup, move an element with the keyboard and play a beep with Web Audio
story: You've entered the Event Belt! Everything here reacts to a signal. Today you'll steer your ship with the **keyboard**, and add a sound on top.

sections.title: keydown and keyup
sections.body:
The moment you press a key a `keydown` event happens, and the moment you let go a `keyup` event happens. To listen to keys on the whole page, we attach the event to `document`. Which key was pressed is in `e.key`:

```js
document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  console.log("Pressed:", e.key);
});
```

| Key | e.key |
|---|---|
| Left / right arrow | `"ArrowLeft"` / `"ArrowRight"` |
| Up / down arrow | `"ArrowUp"` / `"ArrowDown"` |
| Enter | `"Enter"` |
| Space | `" "` (text with a single space) |
| Esc | `"Escape"` |
| Letters and digits | `"a"`, `"A"`, `"1"` |

Click inside the page once first so that it hears the keys.

tasks.title: Key detector
tasks.prompt:
When a key is pressed (`keydown`), write the key's name into the `#key` paragraph like `Key pressed: a`.

The space key's `e.key` value is an invisible `" "`, so write `Space` instead: `Key pressed: Space`.
tasks.html: Click the page and press a key.
tasks.starter: // listen to the keydown event on document

tasks.title: Slide the rocket
tasks.prompt:
The right arrow (`ArrowRight`) adds 20 to `x`, the left arrow (`ArrowLeft`) takes 20 away. `x` always stays **between 0 and 260**.

After every move:

- move the rocket with `transform`: `rocket.style.transform` should look like `translateX(40px)`,
- write `x: 40` into `#pos`.

Call `e.preventDefault()` for the arrows; other keys shouldn't change anything.
hints: x = Math.max(0, Math.min(260, x)); clamps x.

tasks.title: Engine button
tasks.prompt:
The engine runs as long as the space key is held down:

- When space is pressed (`keydown`): the `#engine` text becomes `Engine: ON` and the `on` class is added.
- When space is released (`keyup`): it becomes `Engine: OFF` and the `on` class is removed.

Don't forget to call `e.preventDefault()` for space; other keys must not affect the engine.
tasks.html:
Engine: OFF

Click the page, then hold down the space key.
tasks.starter:
const engine = document.querySelector("#engine");

// listen to keydown and keyup
hints: if (e.key !== " ") return; skips the other keys.
Write two separate listeners: one for keydown, one for keyup.

challenge.title: Secret code
challenge.prompt:
Games have secret codes! Keep the pressed keys in the `pressed` array, but the array should always hold only **the last 4 keys** (`slice(-4)`).

When the last 4 keys are `ArrowUp`, `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowDown` in that order, write `Secret mode unlocked!` into `#secret`.
hints: To compare two arrays, turn them into text: pressed.join(",") === CODE.join(",")

project_task.title: Keyboard control
project_task.prompt:
Let's steer the ship with the arrow keys. Write the `moveShip(dx)` function:

- it changes `x` by `dx` and keeps it **between 0 and `MAX_X` (270)**,
- it places the ship: `ship.style.left = x + "px"`,
- if you like, it plays a sound with the ready-made `beep()` function when the ship hits the wall (optional).

Then listen to `keydown`: the left arrow calls `moveShip(-STEP)`, the right arrow calls `moveShip(STEP)`, and `e.preventDefault()` stops the page from scrolling. The arrows shouldn't move the ship while someone is typing into the pilot name box.
